title: NG3: Decisive counterexample and all equivalence validation rest on an absent, unverifiable check.py

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** solution.tex, Remark 1 (lines 184-201), Proposition 1 (lines 225-230), and the closing attribution (lines 348-351).

**The gap.** The solution central thesis -- "(I) is necessary but NOT sufficient, hence no purely pentagon/hexagon system is complete" (Summary item 2, lines 332-337) -- is supported ONLY by computation that is not in the workspace and cannot be checked:

- the counterexample "x_e=3 for all edges except one edge =5, giving 360 bad internal-internal pairs" (lines 186-193);
- the validation "0 discrepancies for (U) and (G) vs brute force over 505 assignments; 28 for (U) and (I)" (lines 194-197);
- the structural data in Lemma 1 (spectrum, 1260 pentagons, 5250 hexagons) and the uniform-c checks.

Neither check.py nor any output transcript is present (workspace contains only preamble.tex, problem.tex, solution.tex). None of these claims is reproducible or verifiable from the text. For a mathematical proof, the counterexample must be exhibited EXPLICITLY -- name the two internal vertices and their two equal shortest paths, and show the arithmetic tie r+d(a,q)=(x_e-r)+d(b,q) with q internal -- not asserted computationally.

**Consequence.** As written, the load-bearing insufficiency claim, and therefore the rejection of the 5376-equation system in the section On the figure 5376 (lines 310-322), is unverified. This also bears on carried-over gap G2 (rm-05346-3): the solution claimed resolution of G2 (local insufficient) depends entirely on this unverified computation.

**To close.** Either (a) exhibit the counterexample by hand with explicit vertices/paths, or (b) place check.py and a transcript of its output in the workspace and reference them precisely.
